market_implied_expectations:
Under the corrected model's conditional 6.2168482786% WACC and 0.8017374736% terminal growth, the $106.79 price requires CFO-minus-total-cash-capex to grow 16.9744503% annually from LTM $629.879m to FY2030 $1,275.459544m, a 19.6760% cash margin on model revenue. WACC is the blended return assumed for debt and equity; this is a model inference, not an observed market forecast. Alternatively, retaining the engine's base cash path and solving only the required return gives 4.9553250163%. Either single-input solve reproduces $106.79. Consequently the price does not uniquely identify an exceptional cash-growth expectation. [valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 1-2A]
Both solves use 148.333m economic diluted working shares, derived from 153.686m GAAP diluted shares less the disclosed 5.353m note-hedge benefit, with cash-settled principal retained in debt; this is a period-average working count, not an exact current fully diluted count. Strict net debt is $6,082.571m, debt less cash/equivalents, with operating leases excluded. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, balance sheet p.3, Note 7 pp.18-20, Note 13 p.25 and MD&A p.39; valuation/01_price-and-capital-structure.md, Anchor Block]
engine_view:
The engine retains the FY2026-FY2028 consensus revenue anchors, then models $6,115.3m/$6,482.3m revenue in FY2029/FY2030. CFO margins rise from 30.0% to 33.5%, cash capex falls from 20.0% to 18.5% of revenue, and GAAP EBIT margin recovers from 10.5% to 14.0% across FY2026-FY2030. Full-year cash-proxy amounts are $449.1m/$558.7m/$707.8m/$856.1m/$972.3m; the discounted first-year input is a $227.926m H2 stub, not the full-year amount. At the stated rate and terminal growth, the base value is $71.26391017, 33.26724% below the retained price. The base FY2030 cash margin of about 15% is 4.676 percentage points below the reverse path's 19.676%. [valuation/04_intrinsic-dcf.md, sections 1-6; valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, section 2]
The 12-month scenario set is joint execution bull $153.392526 (10%), rate/growth sensitivity bull $113.616526 (15%), base $71.263910 (45%), and cyclical bear $47.295374 (30%). Probabilities total 100%; their weighted target is $78.639103 and expected return -26.360986%. The joint bull requires both stronger cash and the lower required return and implies +43.64%; its probability is judgment, not an empirical frequency. The sensitivity bull and cyclical bear retain the base explicit cash path and change discount/terminal assumptions; they are not independent valuation methods or separately modeled cash outcomes. The $35.22 structural floor has a separate 24-36-month horizon. [final_thesis.md, section 8; decision_record.json, scenarios; valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md, sections 6-7]
what_everyone_knows: Security and Cloud Infrastructure Services (CIS) grew 10% and 39% in Q2 FY2026 while Delivery fell 6%; group revenue rose 5.4%. The same public evidence shows a 55.8% GAAP gross margin, down 331 basis points, and GAAP-derived EBITDA down 18.7%. These are disclosed observations available to other investors. Positive historical cash generation and four observed quarterly revenue/normalized-EPS beats are also visible, so a revenue-growth narrative is not the only public interpretation. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.5, 25 and 30; Supplemental Financial Information, 2nd Quarter 2026.xlsx, Supplemental Metrics sheet; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, section 6; earnings/01_historical-financials.md, sections 1-2]
what_is_priced_in: The retained quote can be explained by a higher cash path, a lower required return, or a combination. The model cannot establish which explanation investors actually use. The near-term consensus bar is close to company guidance and already includes Q3 timing limits, while FY2027-FY2028 estimates anticipate accelerating profit after the FY2026 decline. It would therefore be inaccurate to claim that the next quarterly bar itself proves excessive expectations. The mean analyst target is not the expectation mathematically embedded in today's price. [valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, sections 2-2A; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, sections 2-7; AKAM Estimates Report, Consensus sheet, annual normalized-EPS and EBITDA rows]
what_market_may_be_missing: The engine's possible difference is that Security/CIS revenue growth may consume more capital and operating cost than investors expect, so better revenue mix may fail to produce the required cash return. The latest profit compression, 5.14x strict net leverage and absent category profit/capital/cash disclosures make this a reasonable risk to investigate. They do not demonstrate that consensus has ignored it, nor prove that the fast-growing categories cannot improve group cash generation. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.3, 5, 19, 25 and 30; earnings/99_earnings-synthesis.md, sections 1-5; balance-sheet-survival/99_balance-sheet-survival-synthesis.md, sections 1-5]

base_rate_check:
The proper comparison is cash growth with cash growth. Filing-built FCF, defined as CFO minus cash purchases of property/equipment and capitalized internal-use software, is approximately $618.4m/$833.9m/$699.265m in FY2023/FY2024/FY2025. The module computes a 6.34% FY2023-FY2025 CAGR; the latest LTM $629.879m is 9.92% below FY2025, not a year-on-year comparison to a separately constructed prior LTM. The conditional 16.97% requirement exceeds the two-year realized CAGR by about 10.63 percentage points. This short record raises the evidence burden, but does not make the forward outcome impossible. [FY2025 Form 10-K, pp.54-56; Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, pp.7-8; earnings/01_historical-financials.md, sections 1-2; valuation/05_reverse-dcf.md, section 3]
The mix is changing: group cash history may understate the growing Security/CIS opportunity, while category profit, cash and invested capital are undisclosed, preventing a valid category-level comparison and re-aggregation. Revenue growth and the vendor's loosely labelled LT Growth field cannot substitute for FCF growth. Four quarterly beats are too few for a statistical success probability. The engine itself assumes substantial margin improvement and a falling cash-capex share, so its base is not a simple continuation of deteriorating profitability. [Q2 FY2026 Form 10-Q, segment/category disclosures pp.23-30; earnings/04_guidance-consensus.md, section 6; valuation/04_intrinsic-dcf.md, operating assumptions]
